title: add vpc control plane dns peering security-groups and endpoint automation (terraform + helm)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: enable fully automated provisioning of the Private Control Plane VPC networking surface for private deployments. This PR adds a reusable Terraform module and supporting Helm/installer mappings to provision subnets, VPC endpoints, security groups, cross-account VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone peering so customers can bring a control plane into their VPC with minimal manual networking steps. Summary of changes and rationale: 1) Terraform: new module modules/vpc/control-plane that encapsulates: subnet creation (public/private tags for control-plane-only subnets), configurable AZ distribution, interface and gateway endpoints (SSM, EC2, KMS optional), security groups with least-privilege egress rules, route table associations, VPC peering resource with configurable acceptor account and peer CIDR, and Route53 private hosted zone association/peering resource to wire control-plane DNS into customer VPCs. Module is written to be idempotent and safe for repeated applies; includes explanation in README and examples for multi-account setups. 2) Installer/Helm: expose values.controlPlane.network.{privateDnsZone,peerAccountId,peerVpcId,allowedEgressCidrs} and map those to the terraform provisioner and templates used by the private installer. Helm chart values for the control-plane now accept endpoint overrides and trust anchors used for cross-VPC service discovery. 3) Security and audit: added explicit security group rules that restrict egress to AWS-managed endpoints and to customer-specified CIDRs; KMS key alias creation is guarded and uses the installer KMS module to avoid collisions; CloudTrail integration notes added. 4) Tests: added a sandbox integration test that runs terraform plan/apply against a test AWS account (staged) and validates endpoints and DNS resolution; added unit tests for terraform modules using kitchen-terraform and updated CI to include tflint and checkov scans for the new module. 5) Docs: updated redwood-private-installer/README.md with examples for multi-az, peering, and DNS delegation scenarios.
